title: Well-definedness of the Fourier–Deligne transform
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring in which $p$ is invertible
and whose exponent is invertible on $S$, and let $\pi:V\to S$,
$\pi':V'\to S$, $b$, $\Psi$, $r\in\mathbf Z$ and the projections
$p_1,p_2$ be as in [def-fd-transform], with
$p_2:V\times_SV'\to V'$ of finite type and admitting a compactification.
Assume that $V'$ is of finite type (quasi-compact and locally of finite type) over some field $k$. The compactification implies that $p_2$ is separated. Let
$D^b_c(-,\Lambda)$ denote the full subcategory of the derived category of
étale sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules consisting of the bounded complexes with
constructible cohomology sheaves. Then for every
$K\in D^b_c(V,\Lambda)$,

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\in D^b_c(V',\Lambda),
$$

so that $\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ restricts to a functor

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi:
D^b_c(V,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D^b_c(V',\Lambda).
$$

proof.text: Put $W=V\times_SV'$. The pullback $p_1^*$ in [def-fd-transform] is the exact inverse image on constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves, by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Hence $\mathcal H^i(p_1^*K)=p_1^{-1}\mathcal H^i(K)$ and the same global cohomological bounds hold. The underlying finite sheaves remain constructible by [prop-constructible-pullback]; the inherited module action and the same pulled-back strata make them constructible module sheaves. Thus $p_1^*K\in D^b_c(W,\Lambda)$ in the ordinary étale sense of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].

source.place: Tag 095Y, lemma-pullback-c; finite constant-coefficient exactness and cohomology

proof.text: In the general coefficient convention of [def-fd-transform], the kernel on $W$ is the Artin–Schreier sheaf $\mathcal L_{\Psi,b}$, namely the sheaf $b^*\mathcal L_\Psi$ of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] (current general-coefficient statement) for $k=\mathbf F_p$, the kernel convention that [def-fd-transform] adopts. Apply [lem-fd-artin-schreier-finite-lisse] with $X=W$. Its hypotheses are exactly the characteristic-$p$ condition on $W$, $p\in\Lambda^\times$, finite $\Lambda$, and the specified $b,\Psi$. It gives a flat constructible rank-one module sheaf $\mathcal K_\psi$ without requiring $V$ or $V'$ to be a vector bundle or to come from a finite field.

source.place: Tag 0A3J, section-artin-schreier, exact Artin–Schreier sequence; character-idempotent trivialization as in the argument recorded in report.md

external.place: artinSchreierSheafUpperStarIso, lines 688–692; isLocallyConstantSheaf_artinSchreierSheafOf, lines 731–734; isConstructibleSheaf_artinSchreierSheafOf, lines 1298–1302 (reference statements, not a claim of transitive closure)

proof.text: Apply [lem-fd-flat-constructible-tensor] on $W$ to $p_1^*K$ and the flat constructible sheaf $\mathcal K_\psi$. It gives $M=p_1^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda\mathcal K_\psi[0]\in D^b_c(W,\Lambda)$. In particular this operation has not imposed finite Tor amplitude on $K$; its cohomology remains in the same interval as that of $K$.

source.place: Tag 095I, lemma-tensor-product-constructible, and Tag 0961, lemma-tensor-c; flat degree-zero specialization, with the cohomology computation recorded in report.md

proof.text: Apply [lem-fd-finite-ring-compact-support-finiteness] with $Y=V'$, $X=W$ and $f=p_2$, using the chosen compactification that defines the transform. Here $V'$ is of finite type over the field $k$ by the corrected hypothesis, $p_2$ is of finite type by assumption, and its compactification is supplied. The lemma also verifies separatedness from that compactification. It gives $Rp_{2,!}M\in D^b_c(V',\Lambda)$ for this arbitrary finite ring, including rings that are neither fields nor quotients of discrete valuation rings.

source.place: Tag 0GL0, theorem-constructible-shriek; Tag 0G2A, lemma-derived-lower-shriek-bounded, clause (3); chosen-compactification convention of section-derived-lower-shriek-compactification

proof.text: By [def-fd-transform], $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)=(Rp_{2,!}M)[r]$. If $Rp_{2,!}M$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$, its shift has $\mathcal H^i((Rp_{2,!}M)[r])=\mathcal H^{i+r}(Rp_{2,!}M)$, and so has constructible cohomology in $[a-r,b-r]$. This proves membership in the full subcategory [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The ambient transform is already a functor by [def-fd-transform], including its specified action on morphisms. Restricting a functor whose objects land in a full subcategory retains its maps, identities and composites, giving the asserted functor on $D^b_c$.

proof.text:
The kernel $\mathcal K_\psi$ of [def-fd-kernel] is a lisse
rank-one module, hence of finite Tor amplitude [prop-kernel-lisse] in the
coefficient conventions of the proper-base-change chapter ([def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]). By [prop-functor-package] of the framework chapter, the derived
pullback $Lp_1^*$, the derived tensor product, and the derived
compact-support direct image $p_{2,!}$ (the compact-support direct
image of the separated finite-type $p_2$)
are exact triangulated functors on their constructible and finite-Tor
domains; hence $Lp_1^*K\otimes^L_E\mathcal K_\psi$ lies in
$D^b_c(V\times_SV^\vee,E)$, and its image under $p_{2,!}$
lies in $D^b_c(V^\vee,E)$; the shift $[r]$ of
[def-fd-transform] preserves boundedness and constructibility.

split_report.summary: Repair of return 8c3cde06d6. Replaced the invalid finite-field/adic kernel and functor-package citations by three general finite-ring lemmas. Retained ordinary etale Db_c without requiring finite Tor amplitude of K. Added all category and morphism notions, verbatim citations and unit realization. STATEMENT-DISPUTED: locally finite type target alone does not give global boundedness; restored the quasi-compact target present in the source Lean declaration, with explicit disjoint-affine-space counterexample in report.md.
split_report.blueprint: main-20261015 P2: pullback, lisse flat kernel, tensor, compact support and shift/restriction, in this order. The unit and node omit target quasi-compactness and their proof still uses E and the vector-dual setting: these are source errors, repaired below the unit with the same operations. The corrected statement restores the actual source theorem finite-type target hypothesis.

statement_dispute.reason: The main-20261015 node and unit omit QuasiCompact aV' from the source theorem. Global boundedness fails without it.
statement_dispute.counterexample: Take k algebraically closed of characteristic p, Lambda=F_l with l!=p, S=V'=coprod_{n>=0} Spec k, V=coprod_{n>=0} A^n_k, pi the componentwise structure maps and pi'=id. Then W=V, p1=id, p2=pi is finite type and has compactification coprod A^n -> coprod P^n -> coprod Spec k. Set b=0, Psi=1, r=0 and K=Lambda_V[0]. On component n, H_c^{2n}(A^n,Lambda)=Lambda(-n) is nonzero. Thus Rp2! K is not globally bounded.
statement_dispute.correction: Require V' to be quasi-compact as well as locally of finite type over k, exactly the actual slopmaster2 theorem and its docstring; retain arbitrary finite Lambda, arbitrary pairings and Db_c inputs.

tool_uses.why: Generic exact inverse image of constant-coefficient module sheaves; covers arbitrary schemes and rings, with no finite-field setting.
Generic constructible sheaf pullback along any scheme morphism; underlying finite sheaves give the constructibility used at step 1.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q140-13ac20481 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all five steps, the three new nodes, every cited statement, the unit record, Stacks more-etale 0GL0 (theorem-constructible-shriek), 0G2A(3) and the compactification section, tags 095I, 0961, 095Y and 0A3J, and slopmaster2 FourierTransform/Defs.lean l.290-349. (1) The corrected item statement adds quasi-compactness of V'. The uncorrected blueprint statement is false: with V = ⊔A^n over V' = ⊔Spec k and K = Λ[0], H^{2n}_c of A^n is nonzero on component n, so FT(K) is not globally bounded. The added hypothesis is exactly the Lean `[QuasiCompact aV']` at Defs.lean:315. The only citer, thm-a1-fourier-t-exact, works over A^1 and satisfies it. This corrects a false statement (E7), not a silent weakening, and the maintainer should record it in HUMAN.md. The coefficient category is ordinary small-étale finite Λ, never identified with Q̄_ℓ or E. (2) All three new nodes are true and are not duplicates or restated clauses. The Artin–Schreier lemma follows from a finite étale cover with regular F_p action, on which the image of e_Ψ is free of rank one. The tensor lemma holds because a flat factor makes the derived tensor termwise and constructibility passes to a common refinement. The finiteness lemma: X and Y are Noetherian, f = qj is separated, finite Λ is Noetherian and torsion, so 0GL0 gives constructibility and 0G2A(3) gives a uniform bound N. Edge cases checked: empty X, Λ = 0, trivial Ψ, K = 0, and Z/l against Z/l^2. (3) Batch-5 check on sk-def-as: it is a definition, but its stmt_deps chain into sk-thm-sf-package, a closure of 13,999 nodes with 60 in sec-poincare-duality, and it is the finite-field E-framed definition. The item actually needs def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf, whose main-20261015 statement is the general-Λ definition and which def-fd-kernel's current statement cites. Its closure has 83 nodes and reaches no trace-formula, Poincaré-duality or assumption node. I replaced sk-def-as with it in item step 2 (proof_deps recomputed) and in the statement and stmt_deps of lem-fd-artin-schreier-finite-lisse. No other new citation reaches either chapter. (4) I accept the tool uses of prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact and prop-constructible-pullback. (5) For the maintainer: the unit's realized steps list prop-kernel-lisse, which the item does not use. The unit's P1 route (vector bundle, Q̄_ℓ) does not fit the general item, and the unit statement and uses need reconciliation together with the quasi-compactness source error.
